correctness.rationale: The Markov kernel is exactly specified and takes values in [0,1]. Monotone uniform coupling gives strict W1 contraction. Stationary moments follow from conditional expectation/variance. Positive branch probabilities yield the exact IFS support, with open-set dimension above the gap threshold. At alpha=1/2, a two-sided iid-driven construction ensures an ergodic binary action factor, and the current state is its past binary expansion; SMB plus H(X)<log2 establishes singularity and Pinsker plus exact variance bounds the measure dimension. Nonatomicity follows from a uniformly bounded cylinder probability. A standalone exact-rational implementation checked 550 finite identities. No finite computation is used as an infinite proof.

The related Cao--Cortez 2024 mean-field symmetric branch probability is constant at one half and its alpha=1/2 law is uniform; here the self-action branch probability is the current opinion and the alpha=1/2 law is singular with an explicit entropy deficit. Classical IFS and entropy methods are prior ingredients. value.rationale: Two fixed opposed actions generate a nontrivial stochastic stationary opinion distribution whose support transitions at alpha=1/2. The newly resolved critical law has full interval accessibility but is still singular continuous with a strict explicit entropy-dimension deficit; this contrasts with the fair-branch uniform critical law in a close published model. The variance and contraction rates are exact and depend on interpretable self-trust and learning parameters, providing a motivated analysis of state-feedback opinion fragmentation.
